niche: a survey's translated versions of a twelve-item connectedness scale gated for fieldwork on the share of each version's total-score variance due to the trait, where the negatively worded items carry a wording factor in some translations
answer: Release the Punjabi, Spanish and Persian versions of the BCS-12 for the wave 6 fieldwork, hold the Mandarin, Tagalog, Arabic and Korean versions for cognitive interviews and a second pilot, and send the Cantonese, Urdu and Vietnamese versions back for retranslation.

spine.entity: one interviewer-administered pilot or pretest interview's value for one questionnaire variable

driver: The decisive quantity is the share of a composite's variance due to the one attribute it is meant to capture, and in some versions a subset of its components shares a second source of variance unrelated to the attribute, so the components' average agreement or a single-source fit counts that second source as the attribute and passes versions whose attribute share falls short; only a fit that gives the subset its own source shows the shortfall.
driver_concrete: In six of the ten translated versions of the BCS-12 the six negatively worded items (BCS02, BCS04, BCS06, BCS08, BCS10 and BCS12) share a wording factor (the translation's rendering of negation), so Cronbach's alpha and a one-factor omega count the wording variance as connectedness and release or hold versions whose connectedness share is below the bands; a bifactor model with a wording factor on those six items (or their correlated residuals) gives the trait's share and holds or reworks them.
stump: A competent solver gates each version on Cronbach's alpha (or a one-factor omega) and files 6 of the 10 versions wrong (the Mandarin, Tagalog, Arabic, Vietnamese and Korean versions released and the Cantonese version held); the step that lands it there is taking the score's whole common variance for connectedness when the negatively worded items share a wording factor in those translations.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who builds each version's valid pilot completes, reverse-scores the six negatively worded items, reads the release standard's definition of reliability correctly and estimates it with Cronbach's alpha or a one-factor omega files 6 of the 10 versions wrong, releasing or holding the six wording-affected versions on variance their negatively worded items share with each other and not with connectedness.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the share of the scale score's variance due to the trait (omega hierarchical) under the measurement model each version's item responses support, with a reverse-keyed wording factor separated from the trait; with meters or wards for items there are no negatively worded statements, no translation that changes how negation is answered and no latent trait to separate from a response style, and the task stops making sense.

differentiation.task257: task257 counts a scale's dimensions when lopsided item splits distort Pearson correlations; this build estimates a trait's share of a translated version's score with a reverse-keyed wording factor separated from it.

notes: Seed DQ10: the world, decision and quantity kept; the seed's own pitfall (alpha against congeneric omega) is a wrong rung here: the decisive step is separating a wording factor that alpha and a one-factor omega both count as the trait. G17 decisive (the model the data supports), G16 supporting. Six of ten versions carry the factor; the default path files those six wrong.
